binders: An arbitrary finite index type ι.
An arbitrary measurable sample space Ω.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A family B_i:Ω→Bool indexed by i∈ι.
hypotheses: The index set has positive cardinality, so it is nonempty.
Every B_i is measurable into Bool with its discrete measurable structure.
The indexed family (B_i) is jointly independent under μ.
For every i, the pushforward law of B_i under μ is the fair Bernoulli law on Bool: true and false each have probability 1/2.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001(b)=1 when b=true and LocalDef001(b)=0 when b=false.
LocalDef002 is the Bernoulli PMF on Bool with success probability 1/2, assigning probability 1/2 to true and 1/2 to false.
The law of B_i is expressed as the pushforward measure map(B_i,μ).
The expectation is the real Bochner integral of S with respect to μ.
Variance is ProbabilityTheory.variance, defined as the real conversion of the extended variance.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any nonempty finite collection of jointly independent fair Boolean random variables on a probability space, regard true as 1 and false as 0 and sum these indicators. The sum has expectation equal to half the number of variables and variance equal to one quarter of the number of variables.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition explicitly excludes the empty index set by requiring 0<|ι|, even though the displayed moment formulas would also evaluate correctly for an empty sum.
The conclusion gives only the first two moments of the sum; it does not explicitly assert that the sum has a binomial distribution.
No explicit integrability assumptions appear, but each summand is 0-1 valued and the index set is finite, so the sum is bounded and integrable.
The explicit measurability hypotheses prevent any totalized or exceptional behavior of measure pushforward for nonmeasurable functions.
Variance is obtained from extended variance by toReal; boundedness of the finite sum ensures the variance is finite, so this conversion loses no information.
